claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based alloys exhibit coercivity below 100 Oe and high saturation magnetization.
Untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based HEAs typically have saturation magnetization of about 1.6–1.8 T.
Aging cold-worked FeCoNi-based alloys at 500–700 °C for 4–12 h will induce short-range ordering.
Aging cold-worked FeCoNi-based alloys at 500–700 °C for 4–12 h will induce nanoscale precipitation.
The proposed aging treatment can maintain a primarily fcc matrix while producing localized ordering or fine precipitates.
Approximately 30–50% cold work followed by the proposed aging treatment can yield a final grain size near or below 200 nm.
Nanoscale precipitates or short-range ordered domains in the fcc matrix provide domain-wall pinning sites.
Short-range ordering and fine precipitates locally enhance magnetic inhomogeneity.
The resulting magnetic inhomogeneity raises domain-wall pinning energy.
Preserving much of the fcc matrix will preserve its high saturation magnetization.
The intervention will raise coercivity above 100 Oe relative to the sub-100 Oe baseline.
The intervention will limit the reduction in saturation magnetization to less than approximately 15%.
Keeping the aging temperature below approximately 750 °C will avoid extensive secondary-phase formation.
The hypothesis is restricted to near-equiatomic FeCoNi compositions or slight variants.
Room-temperature hysteresis measurements to at least 5000 Oe will quantify coercivity and saturation magnetization.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mediator posit precipitate formation, while the experiment asks investigators to confirm a single-phase fcc structure. Distinct precipitates normally imply more than one phase unless they are explicitly defined as coherent ordering within the same crystallographic phase.

The design specifies confirmation of a single-phase fcc structure, whereas the falsification rule only requires the alloy to remain predominantly fcc, leaving inconsistent structural acceptance criteria.
